newsitem.title: MALAWI: PRIVATE MALAWIAN AIR CARGO SERVICE TO START SEPT.
newsitem.headline: PRIVATE MALAWIAN AIR CARGO SERVICE TO START SEPT.

text.p: Malawi's first private international air cargo company, with an initial capital investment of $25 million, will start operating in September, an official said on Friday.
The local director for South-African based Starwelt Trans Lloyd Cargo Limited, Francis Nyrongo, told Reuters that all formalities including an air service permit were in place.
"First week of September, we'll be operational," he said in a telephone interview.
He said Starwelt would operate one CL 44-Canadair aircraft with a cargo capacity of 27 tons and one Boeing 707 with 40 tons capacity from Malawi.
The airline will operate through a seven-member joint venture investment involving two Malawians, one Tanzanian, one American, two Britons and a New Zealander.
Stewart Trans Lloyd has headquarters in South Africa from where it operates several aircraft on international routes.
Nyirongo did not rule out competition from government-run "Air Malawi" which has four aircraft on which it combines passengers and cargo.
"We are optimistic about the market in Malawi since there are no cargo planes in the country and Air Malawi uses passenger planes for cargo," he said.
